about: Eras in which a paper's crossword title prints no setter name, measured on the cached OCR (Gale page reads under archive_org_crops/titles, archive.org pagetext, the Gale TLS page words): a 'by X' / 'Set by X' within the title's neighbourhood was found in none of the pages of the era (noise hits such as 'a poem by John' excluded). A puzzle dated inside an era has no setter to find, so the site does not treat its missing setter as a gap. Written by hand from tools/byline_backfill.py --measure output; series are puzzle series ids.

ftcryptic.measured: GaleFT 1971-87: 1,306 title pages, 0 'Set by'; archive.org FinancialTimes 1971-87: 14 sampled editions a year, 0; 'Set by X' first prints in 1988 (6 of 14 sampled, 'No. 6,798 Set by FRESCA').

tls.measured: Gale TLS page OCR: no 'TLS Crossword N by X' for any No under 894; 'TLS Crossword 894 by Praxiteles' (2011-09-16) is the first, 'TLS Crossword 946 by Tantalus' after.

indysunday.measured: GaleIndependentSunday 1990-2015: no 'by X' beside the title in 1990-98 or 2000-11; only the 1999 'Beelzebub prize crossword' title names its setter, and the Concise 'by Eimi' (2012-13) is another puzzle's.
